instruction: I frequently write Python code in Vim and need proper indentation. Look up online how to enable automatic indentation in Vim and apply this configuration to my local Vim settings permanently.

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

metadata.explanation: Task requires searching for how to enable automatic indentation in Vim, then editing ~/.vimrc to add 'set autoindent' or 'set ai'. The evaluator verifies the .vimrc file contains the auto-indent setting.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks ~/.vimrc for auto-indent configuration using 'set autoindent' or 'set ai'
Shell script properly verifies the permanent configuration by reading the .vimrc file
Data flow is correct: shell script executes -> outputs success message -> metric checks for expected string
Complete coverage: evaluator verifies the core requirement (permanent Vim auto-indent configuration)
Minor limitation: grep pattern '^set autoindent\|^set ai' won't match lines with leading whitespace, though this is uncommon in .vimrc files
Minor limitation: doesn't detect alternative auto-indent methods like 'filetype indent on', but 'set autoindent' is the most direct and common approach
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider updating grep pattern to handle optional leading whitespace: grep -q '^[[:space:]]*set autoindent\|^[[:space:]]*set ai'
Consider adding check for 'filetype indent on' as an alternative auto-indent method, though this is optional as 'set autoindent' is the primary standard
